LanguageData.CM_StationDesc:
Change {PAWN_nameDef}'s caste.

- Commoners expect less from life, but can't do some elite work, stop learning past a skill cap, and can't hold ideoligion roles or royal titles.
- Citizens are ordinary colonists.
- Soldiers stand with citizens but expect as little as commoners. They learn Shooting and Melee faster, but their other skills stop at a cap and they dislike skilled labor. Commoners, citizens and nobles look up to them as the colony's defenders; artisans and scholars look down on them. Anyone capable of violence can enlist.
- Artisans master one craft: they learn it faster, sometimes make better items, and get inspired more often. They expect more and dislike menial work.
- Scholars are learned in research, dark study or medicine: they learn their field faster, work better in it, and get inspired more often. They rank with artisans, expect as much, dislike menial work, and want an impressive room to work in.
- Nobles trade and negotiate better and lift the mood of lower castes nearby. They expect a great deal, need a fine private bedroom, refuse menial work, and need their standing upheld. The colony has one noble seat for every few colonists.

Moving someone down a caste upsets them, unless they only just joined.
